evals.name: redirect
evals.prompt: HomeController in src/main/java/com/example/controllers/HomeController.java redirects GET / to /todo/list. Write a JUnit 5 test that proves the redirect happens and lands on the right path.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest class that configures the Micronaut HTTP client not to follow redirects, exchanges GET / and asserts a 303 SEE_OTHER status with a Location header of /todo/list.
assertions: The test sets micronaut.http.client.follow-redirects to false (via @Property or equivalent configuration) so the client does not follow the redirect
The test uses the Micronaut HttpClient injected with @Client("/") and calls toBlocking()
The test uses client.exchange(...) (not retrieve) so the full HttpResponse is available
The test asserts the response status is HttpStatus.SEE_OTHER
The test asserts the Location header equals /todo/list
No third-party HTTP client (RestAssured, OkHttp, java.net.http) or mocking framework is used

evals.name: controller-html
evals.prompt: hey can you add a test for ContactController? it's under src/main/java/com/example/contacts/. The real repo hits a database so I don't want that in the test, just check the page lists a couple of contacts
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest that GETs /contact/list with Accept: text/html, retrieves the body as a String and asserts the stubbed contacts appear in the HTML. The ContactRepository is replaced by an in-test stub that is scoped to this test class only.
assertions: The stub repository is a @Singleton annotated with @Replaces(ContactRepository.class)
The stub is guarded by @Requires(property = "spec.name", value = "<test class name>") and the test class carries a matching @Property(name = "spec.name", value = "<test class name>")
The request sets .accept(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
The body is retrieved as a String (client.retrieve(request, String.class) or equivalent) and the assertions check for the stubbed contact names in the HTML
Mockito or another mocking framework is not used to replace the repository
The test uses plain @MicronautTest (the embedded server is started) rather than startApplication = false

evals.name: method-validation
evals.prompt: TopicRepository.save has a @NotBlank parameter (src/main/java/com/example/topics/TopicRepository.java). There is no implementation yet. Write a test that fails if someone removes that constraint.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects TopicRepository, calls save("") and save(null) and asserts ConstraintViolationException with assertThrows. A stub implementation is declared inside the test, scoped to it with spec.name + @Requires.
assertions: The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)
TopicRepository is obtained from the context (@Inject field or test-method parameter), not instantiated with new
assertThrows(ConstraintViolationException.class, ...) is used for both an empty string and null
A stub implementation of TopicRepository is provided as a @Singleton guarded by @Requires(property = "spec.name", ...) with a matching @Property(name = "spec.name", ...) on the test class
The test does not call a Validator directly to validate the string; it relies on Micronaut's method-parameter validation on the injected bean

evals.name: json-roundtrip
evals.prompt: Add round-trip JSON tests for the Topic record in src/main/java/com/example/topics/Topic.java: object to JSON and JSON back to object.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects io.micronaut.json.JsonMapper, asserts writeValueAsString(new Topic("1", "...")) equals the compact JSON {"id":"1","name":"..."}, and asserts readValue(json, Argument.of(Topic.class)) equals the expected record.
assertions: The test injects io.micronaut.json.JsonMapper (not com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper)
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)
Serialization is asserted with jsonMapper.writeValueAsString(...) against a compact JSON string with no whitespace after ':' or ','
Deserialization is asserted with jsonMapper.readValue(json, Argument.of(Topic.class)) (or the Class overload) and compared with assertEquals against a Topic instance
The test method declares throws IOException or otherwise handles the checked exception from JsonMapper

evals.name: introspection
evals.prompt: Write a test that guarantees App (src/main/java/com/example/core/App.java) stays introspected — someone keeps deleting the @Introspected annotation by accident.
evals.expected_output: A plain JUnit 5 test (no @MicronautTest) asserting assertDoesNotThrow(() -> BeanIntrospection.getIntrospection(App.class)).
assertions: The test class is NOT annotated with @MicronautTest and does not start an ApplicationContext
The test calls BeanIntrospection.getIntrospection(App.class)
The call is wrapped in assertDoesNotThrow (or the test asserts IntrospectionException is not thrown)
The test does not use Java reflection (App.class.getAnnotation(Introspected.class)) to check for the annotation

evals.name: non-unique-bean
evals.prompt: I have two Calculator beans in src/main/java/com/example/calc/ and injecting Calculator blew up at runtime with NonUniqueBeanException. Write a test so this is caught by the build, and tell me how to make it pass.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects BeanContext and asserts assertDoesNotThrow(() -> beanContext.getBean(Calculator.class)), plus a note that marking one implementation @Primary (or the others @Secondary) makes it pass.
assertions: The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)
The test resolves the type with BeanContext.getBean(Calculator.class) (or ApplicationContext.getBean) inside assertDoesNotThrow
The test does not merely count getBeansOfType(Calculator.class) — it asserts the bare type resolves to a single bean
The response recommends @Primary on one implementation or @Secondary on the other(s) as the fix
No bean is deleted or renamed to make the test pass

evals.name: view-render
evals.prompt: There's a Thymeleaf template at src/main/resources/views/todo/index.html. I want a fast unit test that renders it with an empty todos list and checks the output is an HTML5 document — no HTTP, no server.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects ThymeleafViewsRenderer (or ViewsRenderer), calls render("todo/index", Map.of("todos", List.of()), null), converts the Writable to a String and asserts it starts with <!DOCTYPE html>.
assertions: The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)
The test injects a ViewsRenderer (e.g. ThymeleafViewsRenderer) and calls render("todo/index", <model>, <request or null>)
The Writable returned by render is written to a StringWriter (or equivalent) to obtain the HTML as a String
The test asserts the HTML begins with <!DOCTYPE html> (case-insensitive, leading whitespace tolerated)
No HttpClient, controller or embedded server is involved

evals.name: cookie-redirect
evals.prompt: LocaleController (src/main/java/com/example/locale/LocaleController.java) stores the language the user picks in a cookie. Write a test that posting locale=es sets the locale cookie to es.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest with micronaut.http.client.follow-redirects=false that POSTs a form-urlencoded locale=es to /locale, uses exchange, asserts 303 SEE_OTHER and asserts response.getCookie("locale") is present with value es.
assertions: The test sets micronaut.http.client.follow-redirects to false so the cookie on the 303 response is observed
The request is sent with content type application/x-www-form-urlencoded (MediaType.APPLICATION_FORM_URLENCODED)
The test uses client.exchange(...) to get the full HttpResponse
The test asserts the status is HttpStatus.SEE_OTHER
The test reads the cookie with response.getCookie("locale") and asserts it is present and its value is es

evals.name: redirect-status
evals.prompt: LegacyController has two redirects: /old-pricing and /maintenance. Add tests for both.
evals.expected_output: Two tests with follow-redirects=false: /old-pricing returns 301 MOVED_PERMANENTLY with Location /pricing (HttpResponse.redirect), /maintenance returns 307 TEMPORARY_REDIRECT with Location /status (HttpResponse.temporaryRedirect).
assertions: The test sets micronaut.http.client.follow-redirects to false
/old-pricing is asserted to return HttpStatus.MOVED_PERMANENTLY (301), matching HttpResponse.redirect
/maintenance is asserted to return HttpStatus.TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307), matching HttpResponse.temporaryRedirect
Neither test asserts SEE_OTHER (303) or FOUND (302)
Both tests assert the exact Location header (/pricing and /status)

evals.name: static-secured
evals.prompt: We serve images from src/main/resources/assets/images under /assets/images/** and the app uses Micronaut Security (see application.properties). Add a test that makes sure logo.svg loads for visitors who aren't logged in.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest (server started) that GETs /assets/images/logo.svg anonymously and asserts it succeeds, with security left enabled so the intercept-url-map rule is exercised.
assertions: The test uses @MicronautTest without startApplication = false
The test requests /assets/images/logo.svg through the Micronaut HttpClient
The test asserts success (assertDoesNotThrow around exchange, or HttpStatus.OK)
Security is NOT disabled (no micronaut.security.enabled=false or micronaut.security.filter.enabled=false)
The request carries no credentials (it is anonymous)

evals.name: secured-authenticated
evals.prompt: DashboardController is @Secured(IS_AUTHENTICATED). I want tests showing anonymous users are rejected and a logged-in user sees their username.
evals.expected_output: Security stays enabled. One test asserts an anonymous GET /dashboard throws HttpClientResponseException with 401 UNAUTHORIZED. Another authenticates (e.g. a test-scoped AuthenticationProvider and basic auth, or a generated JWT) and asserts the body contains the username. Test-only beans are scoped with spec.name + @Requires.
assertions: Security is NOT disabled (no micronaut.security.enabled=false or micronaut.security.filter.enabled=false)
The anonymous test asserts HttpClientResponseException with HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED
The authenticated test supplies credentials (basic auth with a test AuthenticationProvider, or a bearer token) and asserts the body contains the username
Any test-only bean (e.g. AuthenticationProvider) is guarded by @Requires(property = "spec.name", ...) with a matching @Property(name = "spec.name", ...) on the test class

evals.name: security-disabled
evals.prompt: ReportController is secured but auth is tested elsewhere. I just want a quick test that GET /reports returns the two reports as JSON — don't bother with login.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest with @Property(name = "micronaut.security.filter.enabled", value = StringUtils.FALSE) that retrieves /reports with the Micronaut HttpClient and asserts the two reports.
assertions: Security is bypassed with micronaut.security.filter.enabled set to false
The property value uses StringUtils.FALSE rather than the literal "false"
No AuthenticationProvider, token or credentials are created for the test
The test retrieves /reports with the Micronaut HttpClient and asserts both reports (e.g. Argument.listOf(Report.class) or JSON content)

evals.name: serde-one-direction
evals.prompt: TopicView (src/main/java/com/example/topics/TopicView.java) is a response-only DTO. Write a test that pins down its serialization contract so nobody accidentally makes it readable from requests or breaks writing it.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) asserting the type is serializable (SerdeIntrospections.getSerializableIntrospection or JsonMapper.writeValueAsString) and that deserialization is NOT supported (assertThrows on getDeserializableIntrospection or readValue).
assertions: The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)
The test asserts TopicView can be serialized (getSerializableIntrospection in assertDoesNotThrow, or writeValueAsString with expected JSON)
The test asserts TopicView can NOT be deserialized (assertThrows around getDeserializableIntrospection or readValue)
Only Micronaut serde APIs are used (JsonMapper / SerdeIntrospections), not Jackson's ObjectMapper

evals.name: json-generic-list
evals.prompt: Our API returns a JSON array of Topic. Write a test that [{"id":"1","name":"Micronaut"},{"id":"2","name":"GraalVM"}] deserializes into a List<Topic>.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that calls jsonMapper.readValue(json, Argument.listOf(Topic.class)) and asserts it equals List.of(new Topic("1", "Micronaut"), new Topic("2", "GraalVM")).
assertions: The test injects io.micronaut.json.JsonMapper
The target type is described with Argument.listOf(Topic.class) (or an equivalent generic Argument), not List.class or a raw type
The test asserts equality against a List of the two expected Topic records
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: serde-metadata
evals.prompt: I don't care what the JSON looks like — I just want the build to fail if someone strips the serde annotation from Topic.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects SerdeIntrospections and asserts getSerializableIntrospection and getDeserializableIntrospection for Argument.of(Topic.class) do not throw.
assertions: The test uses SerdeIntrospections (getSerializableIntrospection / getDeserializableIntrospection) rather than asserting on JSON output
Both directions (serializable and deserializable) are asserted
The checks are wrapped in assertDoesNotThrow
The test does not use Java reflection (Topic.class.getAnnotation / isAnnotationPresent) to look for @Serdeable

evals.name: optional-field
evals.prompt: In Customer (src/main/java/com/example/customers/Customer.java) the email is optional but has to be a valid address when it's there. Write validation tests for email.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) with an injected Validator asserting: null email -> no violations; malformed email -> violations; valid email -> no violations.
assertions: The test injects a Validator (jakarta.validation.Validator or io.micronaut.validation.validator.Validator) instead of building one with Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory()
A Customer with a valid name and a null email produces NO violations
A Customer with a malformed email produces violations
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: not-blank-variants
evals.prompt: Test that an Article must have a title.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) with an injected Validator asserting violations for a null, empty and whitespace-only title.
assertions: The test asserts violations for a null title
The test asserts violations for an empty string title
The test asserts violations for a whitespace-only title
The test injects a Validator from the context and uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: missing-introspection
evals.prompt: Write a test that Payment (src/main/java/com/example/payments/Payment.java) rejects a negative amount.
evals.expected_output: The agent notices Payment has no @Introspected (or @Serdeable), so Micronaut's validator has no metadata for it, adds the annotation (or tells the user it is required), and writes a test asserting violations for a negative amount.
assertions: The response or change identifies that Payment needs @Introspected (or @Serdeable) for Micronaut validation to work, and adds it or explicitly tells the user to
The test injects a Validator from the context (no Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory())
The test asserts a non-empty set of violations for a negative amount
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: violation-path
evals.prompt: Test that an Address with a blank city fails validation — and that it's the city that fails, not some other field.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) building an Address with valid street and postalCode and blank city, asserting exactly one violation whose property path is city.
assertions: The Address is built with valid street and postalCode so only city is invalid
The test asserts on the violation's property path (getPropertyPath()) being city
The test asserts there is exactly one violation (size 1) or that every violation is on city
The test injects a Validator and uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: absent-bean
evals.prompt: SmsSender (src/main/java/com/example/sms/SmsSender.java) must not be created unless SMS is turned on. Write a test that it's absent by default.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that injects BeanContext and asserts assertFalse(beanContext.containsBean(SmsSender.class)) without setting sms.enabled.
assertions: The test asserts absence with containsBean(SmsSender.class) returning false
The test does not set sms.enabled
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) or a manually run ApplicationContext closed with try-with-resources
The test does not inject SmsSender directly (which would fail context setup rather than assert absence)

evals.name: stereotype
evals.prompt: Every service annotated with @AuditedService must end up audited. Write a test that PaymentService carries @Audited.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) that gets beanContext.getBeanDefinition(PaymentService.class) and asserts hasStereotype(Audited.class) (or getAnnotationNameByStereotype(Audited.class).isPresent()).
assertions: The test reads annotation metadata from Micronaut (BeanDefinition or BeanContext.getBeanDefinition), not from Java reflection
The test checks Audited with hasStereotype or getAnnotationNameByStereotype (hasAnnotation alone would miss a meta-annotation)
The test does not use PaymentService.class.getAnnotation / isAnnotationPresent (Audited has CLASS retention so reflection would not see it)
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false)

evals.name: requires-property
evals.prompt: SmsSender is only created when sms.enabled is true. Write a test that it IS available once SMS is turned on.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) annotated with @Property(name = "sms.enabled", value = StringUtils.TRUE) asserting containsBean(SmsSender.class) is true (or getBean does not throw).
assertions: The test sets sms.enabled to true for the context (@Property on the test class, or ApplicationContext.run(Map.of("sms.enabled", ...)))
The property value uses StringUtils.TRUE rather than the literal "true" (when set via @Property)
The test asserts presence via containsBean returning true or getBean in assertDoesNotThrow
The test does not start the embedded server (startApplication = false or a plain ApplicationContext)

evals.name: environments
evals.prompt: Our repository tests use @MicronautTest(environments = "h2") (see BookRepositoryTest). Add a test checking which environments are actually active in that setup.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(environments = "h2") that injects ApplicationContext and asserts getEnvironment().getActiveNames() equals Set.of("test", "h2") (or contains both).
assertions: The test is annotated with @MicronautTest(environments = "h2")
The test reads applicationContext.getEnvironment().getActiveNames()
The assertion expects both test and h2 (exact Set.of("test", "h2") or contains both)
The test does not assume h2 replaces test (i.e. does not assert the set is exactly {"h2"})

evals.name: context-without-test
evals.prompt: We don't have micronaut-test on the classpath, only plain JUnit (see build.gradle). Write a test that GreetingService is a bean and greets correctly.
evals.expected_output: A plain JUnit 5 test that starts ApplicationContext.run() in try-with-resources, asserts containsBean(GreetingService.class) and calls getBean(GreetingService.class).greet(...).
assertions: The test does not use @MicronautTest or any io.micronaut.test import
The ApplicationContext is started with ApplicationContext.run() in a try-with-resources block (or closed in @AfterAll/@AfterEach)
GreetingService is obtained from the context (getBean), not instantiated with new
The test does not add micronaut-test to build.gradle

evals.name: view-handlebars
evals.prompt: We use Handlebars for views. Write a fast test that renders views/home.hbs with title "Hello" and checks the title shows up — no HTTP.
evals.expected_output: A @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) in package com.example.home (or another com.example package) that injects HandlebarsViewsRenderer (or ViewsRenderer), renders "home" with Map.of("title", "Hello"), writes the Writable to a String and asserts it contains Hello.
assertions: The test injects HandlebarsViewsRenderer (or a generic ViewsRenderer), NOT ThymeleafViewsRenderer
The test calls render("home", <model with title Hello>, <request or null>)
The test asserts the rendered output contains Hello
The test uses @MicronautTest(startApplication = false) and no HttpClient
The test lives in a com.example package, not a package copied from the skill's examples (e.g. com.micronauttodo.views)
